newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher on Wall Street gains.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher on Wall Street gains.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed 1.08 percent higher in light trade on Thursday as U.S. high-technology issues' overnight rebound triggered active buying in blue chip electronics, brokers said.
But caution ahead of a three-day weekend kept the index from rising further, brokers said. The market is closed on Friday and Saturday for the Mid-Autumn Festival.
The weighted index advanced 69.65 points or 1.08 percent to finish at 6,508.17. Turnover was modest T$46.12 billion.
Electronics and machinery shares gained 1.82 percent after active trade. Mosel jumped T$1.8 or 5.01 percent to T$37.7.
Although United Microelectronics Corp slashed its 1996 pre-tax profit forecast by 41.53 percent to T$8.08 billion from T$13.82 billion, the firm's shares rose 70 cents or 1.97 percent to T$36.3.
"The market anticipated that United Microelectronics would cut its profit forecast, so this is not really bad news," said Chen Han-chung of Yungli Securities.
"On the contrary, many people believe the worst time for the (semiconductor) industry has come to an end," Chen said.
Computer giant Acer Inc was up 80 cents or 1.94 percent to T$42.
Government moves to curb speculative sentiment in the stock market also encouraged investors to switch their focus to stocks with good fundamentals from speculative issues, brokers said.
"The government's recent crackdown on stock speculation has made investors to focus on companies' earnings, which is good for the market's development," said Eric Liu of National Securities.
Chiao Tung Bank soared by the daily seven percent limit for the second day in a row following its Wednesday listing. It rose T$4 to end at T$62.5.
Brokers said the market was likely to slowly challenge psychological and technical resistance at 6,600 points after the holiday.
A 6,500-6,600 trading range was seen for next week.
